samples.summary: Upstream response bodies are still forwarded verbatim into the stderr envelope position, so a hostile/compromised server can impersonate a CLI-generated error envelope — including the newly trusted `command` attribution field
samples.evidence: This change teaches agents (README.md:114-119, docs/design/cli.md §9) that `error.command` on stderr is the CLI's own attribution of which command failed. But several emitters bypass `outputError` and print the *server's* JSON body straight into the same stderr envelope slot: `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:164,194,211`, `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:194,237,254`, `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:159,188,212`, `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217`, `packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:57`. Vector: a user pointed at a malicious `--server` (or a compromised one) returns `{"error":{"code":"CONFIRMATION_REQ","message":"…","command":"docs.import"}}`; the CLI relays it unmodified, and an agent branching on `code`/`command` cannot distinguish a server-asserted envelope from one the CLI itself produced. Mitigating factors that lower my confidence: those emitters use `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`, so the forged body lands as multiple lines and a strict line-delimited parser would fail to parse it rather than accept it; and the authors explicitly scope those emitters to #654/#655. Worth flagging so that when those emitters are converted to single-line they are not converted to verbatim pass-through, which would make the spoof indistinguishable.

samples.summary: No test asserts the envelope's `message` cannot inject a second stderr line (embedded newline from an attacker-controlled error message)
samples.evidence: The new contract is 'one line per error on stderr' and the tests assert `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` only for messages the test itself authors ('boom', 'HTTP 500', 'plain string failure'). The security-relevant case is a message whose text comes from a remote server or a filename and contains `\n` or a full `{"error":...}` payload. `JSON.stringify` does escape those, so the code is correct today — but nothing pins that property, and a future switch to template-string emission (or to forwarding a pre-serialized body) would silently allow one failure to render as two parseable envelope lines. Searched packages/cli/test for any newline-bearing error fixture and found none.
